title: Fix alert_interval migration ORM breakage
summary: Fixed the `alert_interval` Alembic migration (`0d2efdd3920a`) which imported the `DBAlertRule` ORM model to query and update rows mid-migration. As the ORM model evolved with new columns (e.g. `policy_alert_rule_id`), SQLAlchemy would generate SELECTs referencing columns that don't yet exist at that point in the migration chain, breaking fresh database bootstraps with `UndefinedColumn` errors. The fix replaces all ORM queries with raw SQL `UPDATE` statements decoupled from the evolving model. A Docker Compose smoke test CI job was also added to catch migration failures like this in the future.
userImpact: Fresh database bootstraps (`alembic upgrade head`) now complete successfully without `UndefinedColumn` errors caused by the alert_interval migration.

title: Submit compliance jobs when policy assignments are created
summary: Compliance check jobs are now automatically triggered when policy assignments are created, when alert or attestation rules are created/updated/deleted, and when attestations are submitted. A `raise_on_empty` parameter was added to `check_policy_compliance` so that rule CRUD on policies with no assignments is a silent no-op, while the explicit check endpoint still raises an error. API mutations and compliance job submissions are now committed atomically in a single transaction.
userImpact: Users now receive an immediate `compliance_job_id` when creating policy assignments, and compliance checks are automatically triggered on rule changes and attestation submissions — eliminating the need to manually initiate compliance checks after these operations.

A new `execute_webhook_with_context` method was added to `WebhookExecutor` to support compliance-specific template rendering, filtering context to only non-compliant rules.
userImpact: Users with configured policy webhooks now receive automatic notifications when an assignment becomes non-compliant (after any enforcement delay), and can see the `last_violation_notified_at` timestamp on policy assignment API responses.

title: Policy assignment endpoints with materialization and authz
summary: Implements full CRUD API endpoints for policy assignments, attestations, and compliance status with SpiceDB-based authorization. Policy assignment creation materializes alert rules on each target model and enforces dual permission checks (on the policy and on each target model). The architecture splits the monolithic policies operator/repository into per-resource pairs (PolicyAssignmentsOperator/Repository, AttestationsOperator/Repository), with cross-resource logic like alert rule materialization and cascade deletion handled at the operator level. Adds input validation for group/webhook existence and alert rule SQL queries on policy create/update, duplicate assignment detection (409), model existence validation (404), and a comprehensive end-to-end lifecycle test. Also cherry-picks compliance job improvements (detailed compliance status model with per-rule results, created_at filters, data plane permissions).
userImpact: Users can now create, list, and delete policy assignments to models (with automatic alert rule materialization), record and query attestations per assignment or model with filtering by latest/valid status, and set detailed compliance status including per-rule results — all protected by fine-grained authorization checks. Policy and attestation responses now return full user objects instead of just user IDs.

title: Add NEEDS_ATTENTION compliance status for enforcement delay period
summary: Introduces a new `NEEDS_ATTENTION` compliance status for policy assignments that have rule violations but are still within the enforcement delay grace period. This status is informational only — no webhooks or tags are triggered — giving model owners time to remediate before the system automatically promotes to `NON_COMPLIANT` once the delay expires. The technical design documentation is updated to reflect the new enum value, evaluation logic, compliance metrics class labels, and job lifecycle changes.
userImpact: Model owners now see a `NEEDS_ATTENTION` compliance status during the enforcement delay grace period, giving them clear, early warning of policy violations and time to remediate before full `NON_COMPLIANT` enforcement actions (webhooks, tags) are triggered.

title: Implement policy alert and attestation rule CRUD with authz and propagation
summary: Implements full CRUD endpoints for policy alert rules and policy attestation rules, including static SQL validation for alert rules, live propagation of changes to materialized alert rules on assigned models, and SpiceDB authorization enforcement on all new endpoints. The architecture is refactored to split rule logic into dedicated `PolicyRulesRepository` and per-rule-type operators, and the integration test suite is consolidated into a single `test_policy_full_lifecycle` covering the entire policy workflow from creation through rule management, assignments, compliance, and deletion.
userImpact: Users can now create, list, read, update, and delete policy alert rules and attestation rules via the API, with changes to alert rules automatically propagated to all models the policy is assigned to, and proper authorization checks enforced on every operation.
author: videetparekh1995

title: Policy CRUD (Create/Read/Update/Delete) with Inline Rules
summary: Implements full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) for policies with inline alert and attestation rules. Adds a `PoliciesRepository` supporting atomic policy creation with inline rules, eager-loaded retrieval, paginated listing with name filter and sort, partial updates, and cascade deletes. A `PoliciesOperator` wraps repository calls with transaction commits, and five router endpoints (POST, GET list, GET by ID, PATCH, DELETE) are wired to real operator calls with SpiceDB permission checks enforced. Twelve policy endpoints were removed from the authz whitelist now that proper permission checks are in place. Comprehensive API endpoint lifecycle tests cover the full CRUD flow, validation, filtering, sorting, and error cases using the generated client.
userImpact: Users can now create, list, retrieve, update, and delete policies with inline alert and attestation rules through fully functional API endpoints with enforced permission checks.
author: videetparekh1995

title: Add an alert rule validation endpoint without modelId requirement
summary: Adds a new alert rule validation endpoint that does not require a modelId parameter. The endpoint is whitelisted from authorization checks (authz) while still requiring authentication (authn), allowing users to validate alert rule configurations without needing to specify a model. Supporting changes include new validation logic, query modifier updates, and corresponding unit tests.
userImpact: Users can now validate alert rule configurations without needing to provide a modelId, simplifying the validation workflow for alert rules that are not yet associated with a specific model.

title: Add policy ORM models, database relationships, and migration
summary: Introduces new SQLAlchemy ORM models and an Alembic migration for the policy governance system: `policies`, `policy_alert_rules`, `policy_attestation_rules`, `policy_model_assignments`, and `attestation_records` tables. Adds nullable foreign keys to the existing `alert_rules` table to link materialized alert rules back to their policy source, with a check constraint ensuring referential consistency. Also extends the `AuthZRelationship` enum with `POLICY_PARENT` and `MODEL_PARENT` for dual-parent SpiceDB relationships on policy-model assignments, and validates compliance status (`Pending`, `Compliant`, `Non-compliant`, `Needs Attention`) at the API level rather than via a database constraint.
userImpact: Users will be able to create and manage governance policies that attach alert and attestation rules to models, track per-model compliance status, and have materialized alert rules linked back to their policy source.

title: UP-2756: Enforce lowercase emails
summary: Fixed a bug where pending role invitations were never granted to users with uppercase letters in their emails. The issue occurred because Keycloak stores all emails as lowercase, but pending invitations didn't enforce lowercase normalization. This inconsistency caused email matching to fail during the accept-invites flow. The fix normalizes all user emails to lowercase across the platform, matching Keycloak's behavior and ensuring consistent email storage.
userImpact: Users with uppercase letters in their email addresses can now successfully accept pending role invitations during sign up.
author: alex380125

title: UP-2752: Aggregation time segmentation performance protections
summary: Adds validation checks during aggregation processing to ensure segmentation columns meet performance requirements: fewer than 3 columns, appropriate data types, and limited unique values. These protections are now enforced at metric calculation job time before aggregations execute, rather than during aggregation execution itself, providing a consistent safety mechanism for all aggregation implementations including future custom metrics.
userImpact: Users will now receive clear errors if aggregation segmentation columns fail to meet performance requirements (more than 3 columns, incorrect data types, or excessive unique values) before metric calculation begins, preventing silent failures and performance degradation.

title: UP-2203 data plane version safety
summary: Adds exception handling to the data plane's job agent to gracefully handle job specs with unknown or unsupported types. This change implements automatic deletion of superseded versions to keep the metrics tables lean and performant.

summary: Fixed a bug where user deletion flow failed to delete relationships in SpiceDB due to SQLAlchemy's object reference management. The issue occurred because `db_manager.flush()` moves objects from memory to the transaction buffer, causing the SpiceDB delete queue to be unexpectedly emptied even though deletions hadn't been committed. The fix enqueues copies of deleted objects instead of the objects themselves, ensuring deletions succeed even when `flush()` is called.
userImpact: Users can now be successfully deleted from groups, with their relationships properly removed from SpiceDB.

userImpact: Users can now aggregate and analyze inference counts grouped by predicted class for binary classification models, with support for both direct prediction columns and threshold-based prediction generation from float scores.

userImpact: Aggregation jobs will now fail early with clear validation errors if segmentation arguments don't meet performance requirements (column count, data type, or unique value limits), preventing expensive runtime failures during metric calculation.

summary: Fixed a TypeError in duplicate user email error handling that occurred in AWS with real Keycloak instances. The error handling code was comparing a bytes object to a string, causing the duplicate user detection to fail. Error message comparison now correctly handles the bytes-like error response from Keycloak.
userImpact: Users attempting to create duplicate accounts now receive the proper error response instead of a TypeError when using AWS with real Keycloak authentication.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-2447: Handle non-iterable in filters gracefully
summary: Fixed a crash in the connector filter logic when encountering non-iterable values during filter processing. The connector_read_filters.py module now gracefully handles these edge cases instead of raising an exception, improving robustness of data plane operations.
userImpact: Users can now read data from connectors without encountering errors when filter values are non-iterable.

title: UP-2445 create raw data reader role
summary: A new "Raw Data Reader" role has been created to allow Workspace Read All users to also view raw data independently. This is a new role in the authorization system that can be bound to multiple resource types, with corresponding updates to the SpiceDB schema and comprehensive unit tests added to ensure the multi-resource binding works correctly.
userImpact: Admins can now grant users a Raw Data Reader role to independently grant raw data access alongside existing workspace or project-level permissions.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-2436 fix redis connections in AWS
summary: Redis Python client v6 introduced a breaking change setting `ssl_check_hostname` to `True` by default, which caused Redis connections in AWS to fail with a certificate verification error. This fix disables `ssl_check_hostname` to restore compatibility with AWS deployments.
userImpact: Redis connections in AWS environments now work correctly after the Redis Python v6 upgrade.
author: ianmcgraw

title: Update dependency boto3 to v1.38.10
summary: Updated boto3 dependency from v1.38.9 to v1.38.10. This patch release includes improvements to EC2 volume initialization, ServiceCatalog API validation, and Timestream endpoint support.
userImpact: Users gain access to improved EBS Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization, stricter ServiceCatalog idempotency token validation, and enhanced Timestream dualstack endpoint support.

title: UP-2383 fix ownership of upsolve execute patches directory in ECS
summary: Fixed ownership of the upsolve execute patches directory in ECS environments. The `/db-patches` directory was created with root permissions instead of being owned by the upsolve user, causing permission denied errors when the application tried to read and write executed patch tracking files.
userImpact: Users running upsolve in ECS will no longer encounter permission errors when processing database patches.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-2383 upgrade upsolve
summary: Upgraded upsolve dependency to include backend and theme fixes, plus read-only support. The upgrade addresses BE stability issues and UI improvements without requiring data re-export due to API-only changes in this release.
userImpact: Users benefit from improved backend reliability, theme rendering fixes, and the ability to use read-only mode with upsolve.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-2423: Handle failure to load datasets in metrics calculation jobs
summary: Added graceful handling for dataset load failures in metrics calculation jobs. Previously, when a dataset failed to load, metrics configured to run on that dataset would fail with a generic KeyError, obscuring the root cause. Now the system tracks which datasets failed to load and skips metrics calculation for those datasets, while providing clear error messages to users about why metrics weren't calculated.
userImpact: Users now see clear, actionable error messages when metrics fail due to dataset load failures, instead of generic KeyError exceptions that mask the underlying problem.
author: alex380125

title: UP-2425: Add datetime information to task connection info
summary: Added datetime information to task connection info, including creation and modification timestamps. This change includes a database migration to add time-related columns to the connection info schema and updates to the task API models and repositories to track and manage this temporal data.
userImpact: Users can now view when task connections were created and last modified, enabling better audit trails and troubleshooting of task connection changes.
author: alex380125

title: UP-2427 refresh keycloak token during user invite call
summary: Fixed an issue where the user invite API call would fail when the Keycloak token was expired or not yet initialized, which could occur on server startup. The Keycloak client now refreshes the token before making the user invite call to ensure a valid token is always available.
userImpact: User invite calls will no longer fail due to expired or missing Keycloak tokens on server startup.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-2426 dashboard edit rbac

userImpact: Administrators can now control which roles have access to edit dashboards through RBAC policies, providing more granular permission management.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-2424: Fix regeneration failures
summary: Fixed a regression in connection secret regeneration that was introduced when adding support for deleting connection info in the control plane. The issue was caused by AWS Secrets Manager's scheduled deletion behavior interfering with secret regeneration logic, even when using ForceDeleteWithoutRecovery.
userImpact: Connection secret regeneration now completes successfully without failures.

userImpact: Users gain access to new hash expiration commands and improved security defaults, but must review breaking changes including mandatory retry configuration for cluster clients and removal of deprecated parameters.

The design introduces a priority system (USER_FACING, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) to support operations like moving jobs to the front of the queue and clarifies how job clones are tracked across retries and reruns.
userImpact: Users can now understand and rely on predictable job queue behavior including the ability to prioritize urgent jobs, cancel running jobs with clear state transitions, and track job lineage across retries.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-1582 | Remove task_name from allowed shield filters
summary: Removed the `task_name` filter from the allowed filtering fields in the Shield connector to prevent unintended access to other tasks' data. The Shield API combines filters with AND logic, so the `task_name` filter posed a security risk when exposed to users.
userImpact: Users can no longer filter Shield inferences by task_name, ensuring they can only access data from their current task.

title: UP-1493: Scripts to generate expel sample tabular dataset in s3

userImpact: No direct user impact

userImpact: Users can now join datasets with conflicting column names by using column aliases, and the API provides strongly-typed schema models for UI schema editing instead of opaque serialized data.

title: changed CSP configs

title: UP-3225: Don't overwrite CSP header on dev

The fix introduces an entrypoint script that conditionally applies CSP header configuration based on the deployment environment, ensuring dev environments retain their CSP configuration.
userImpact: Developers can now safely deploy to dev environments without their CSP headers being unintentionally overwritten, preventing CSP-related security and functionality issues in development.

title: unsafe inline into scope
summary: Updated nginx.conf to scope the unsafe-inline directive more precisely. This change improves the Content Security Policy configuration to be more targeted and secure.

author: martin452

title: Explicit CSP in nginx header

userImpact: Web traffic is now served with an explicit CSP header, strengthening security posture against content injection attacks.
author: martin452

title: [UP-3217] fix: modify style-src-elem and script-src-elem
summary: Modified the Content Security Policy directives `style-src-elem` and `script-src-elem` in the Vite configuration. This change addresses CSP enforcement for inline styles and scripts, ensuring stricter security controls are properly configured.
