userImpact: Users will experience significantly faster response times when creating or retrieving role bindings, with expected latency improvements of 20-30x in production environments (from ~6s to sub-300ms).

Modified the job dequeuing logic to filter jobs based on agent memory capacity (passed in POST request), and refactored JobsRepository.submit_job to accept a struct of arguments with sensible defaults for internal fields like retry count and timestamps.
userImpact: Job agents can now declare their available memory capacity and receive only jobs matching that constraint, enabling safer multithreaded job execution and laying groundwork for future scheduling optimizations.

While spawn introduces a slight performance overhead (~2 minutes), it significantly improves test stability by eliminating frequent step restarts.

This rule ensures type imports are properly separated from value imports, improving code consistency and allowing for better tree-shaking. Updated lint commands to support the new rule configuration.
userImpact: Developers will now see linting errors for type imports that don't follow the consistent-type-imports pattern, ensuring cleaner and more optimizable TypeScript code.
author: michalarthurai

title: Fix: Re-enable amplitude session replay tracking
summary: Session replay tracking was being globally disabled due to an explicit removal call in the landing page initialization, preventing replay data collection across the entire stack. This fix re-enables session replay tracking in the platform environment by explicitly configuring it in the Amplitude initialization, following Amplitude's recommended pattern for environment-specific tracking control.
userImpact: Users visiting platform.arthur.ai will now have their sessions recorded in Amplitude session replay, while landing page visitors (arthur.ai) will continue to have replay disabled.
author: pranavarthur

title: fix(migration): build FK indexes before deletes; verbose logging
summary: Migration `b7c9066eca19_remove_compliance_schedules` was stalling on production for 40+ minutes per delete batch due to missing indexes on foreign key columns, forcing sequential scans across millions of rows for cascade delete verification. The fix creates `ix_job_errors_job_run_id` and `ix_job_logs_job_run_id` indexes before deletion begins, enabling index-backed FK constraint verification instead of table scans. Batch performance improves from minutes to sub-second completion.
userImpact: Database migrations that remove compliance schedules now complete in minutes rather than hours, eliminating production migration stalls.
author: videetparekh1995

title: fix(migration): batch compliance job deletes outside transaction
summary: Fixed a database migration that was causing RDS stalls by running unbounded DELETE operations on the unindexed `jobs.kind` column in a single transaction. The migration now batches deletes in groups of 100 outside the transaction boundary, with a temporary index to optimize query performance and enable safe re-runs.
userImpact: Database migrations now complete reliably without stalling RDS, allowing users to upgrade without service degradation.
author: videetparekh1995

title: Update dependency authlib to v1.7.1

summary: Migrated the project from requirements.txt and poetry to uv for dependency management across app-plane and arthur-client. This change enables pinned dependencies, simplifies the dev process, and provides improved performance through uv's optimized resolution and installation.
userImpact: Developers can now use uv sync for consistent, reproducible dependency installation with pinned versions across local development and CI/CD pipelines.
author: nori2

title: Implement policy alert and attestation rule CRUD with authz and propagation
summary: Implements complete CRUD operations for policy alert rules and attestation rules with SpiceDB authorization enforcement and live propagation to materialized alert rules. Alert rule changes automatically propagate to all materialized `DBAlertRule` rows across assigned models, while both rule types enforce permission checks and validate business logic (e.g., preventing deletion of the last rule on an applied policy). The implementation consolidates rule logic into dedicated repositories and operators for maintainability.
userImpact: Users can now create, read, update, and delete policy alert rules and attestation rules through REST APIs, with automatic propagation of alert rule changes to all models and authorization enforcement ensuring only permitted users can manage these rules.
author: videetparekh1995

title: Policy CRUD (Create/Read/Update/Delete) with Inline Rules
summary: Implemented complete Policy CRUD functionality with atomic creation of policy + inline alert/attestation rules, eager-loaded retrieval, paginated listing with filtering/sorting, partial updates, and cascade deletion. All 5 policy endpoints (POST, GET list, GET by ID, PATCH, DELETE) are now wired to real operator calls with SpiceDB permission checks enforced, replacing previous stub implementations and removing 12 endpoints from the authz whitelist.
userImpact: Users can now create, read, update, and delete policies with inline alert and attestation rules through fully secured API endpoints that enforce role-based access control.
author: videetparekh1995

title: Add an alert rule validation endpoint without modelId requirement
summary: Added a new alert rule validation endpoint that validates alert rule configurations without requiring a modelId parameter. This enables users to validate alert rule syntax and constraints independently of model context, with the endpoint properly whitelisted from authorization checks while maintaining authentication requirements.
userImpact: Users can now validate alert rule configurations without needing to specify a model ID, making it easier to test and validate rules before deployment.
author: artur-arthur-ai

title: Add policy ORM models, database relationships, and migration
summary: Introduces a complete policy management system with five new database tables (`policies`, `policy_alert_rules`, `policy_attestation_rules`, `policy_model_assignments`, `attestation_records`) and ORM models for governance workflows. Extends `DBAlertRule` with foreign keys to link materialized alert rules back to their source policies, and adds `POLICY_PARENT` and `MODEL_PARENT` to the SpiceDB authorization relationship enum to support dual-parent policy assignments. Includes a comprehensive Alembic migration with explicit constraint naming for rollback safety.
userImpact: Organizations can now define org-scoped policies, attach alert and attestation rules with compliance tracking, assign policies to models with materialization, and maintain an immutable audit log of attestation actions.
author: videetparekh1995

title: Use oidc
summary: Migrated authentication from access keys to OIDC across all deployment environments. This change improves security by leveraging OpenID Connect for authentication instead of managing static access keys, with verification steps added to validate account access.
userImpact: Users and systems can now authenticate using OIDC tokens instead of access keys, providing enhanced security and simplified credential management across all deployment platforms.

userImpact: Dependency updates are now delayed by 3 days after release, reducing exposure to newly-published malicious or broken package versions.

title: Atomic policy creation with inline rules and field renames
summary: Policy creation now supports inline alert and attestation rules at creation time, with at least one rule required. The create endpoint response is simplified to PolicySummary (id, name, description). Field names have been standardized: `grace_period_days` → `enforcement_delay_days`, `grace_period_ends_at` → `enforcement_starts_at`, and `interval_days` → `validity_period_days` across all policies resources.
userImpact: Users can now create policies with rules in a single atomic operation, eliminating the previous two-step process, and work with clearer, more consistent field naming throughout the policies API.

summary: Fixed a bug where pending invitation grants were failing for users with uppercase letters in their email addresses. This ensures safeguards are applied consistently across aggregations and prevents misuse of the segmentation tag hint.
userImpact: Users will now receive clear validation errors during metric calculation if aggregation segmentation arguments don't meet performance requirements, preventing runtime failures and enabling safe custom metrics with built-in segmentation protections.

title: UP-1893 fix schema inference and metrics calculation on cols with spaces
summary: Fixed schema inference and metrics calculation for columns with spaces in their names. Nested columns like "MA History" were not being properly quoted when rendering SQL, causing inference and aggregation jobs to fail. Applied proper SQL identifier escaping across schema inference, all aggregation functions, and related data retrieval code.
userImpact: Datasets with column names containing spaces can now be properly analyzed with schema inference and metrics calculations working correctly.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-1890 fix raw data retrieval with nans
summary: Fixed raw data retrieval for Expel by encoding NaN values as strings instead of invalid JSON NaN symbols. The frontend cannot parse NaN in JSON, so this change ensures the data is properly serialized and can be correctly consumed by the frontend.
userImpact: Raw data retrieval now works correctly for datasets containing NaN values, enabling proper frontend display of this data.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-1798: Support updating users
summary: Split the user `name` field into separate `first_name` and `last_name` fields in the database and Keycloak configuration to align with Keycloak's data model and enable reliable PATCH requests to update user profiles. Service accounts and data plane accounts store their full name in `first_name` only. Also adds support for correctly setting the `picture` attribute in the database.
userImpact: Users and applications must now use `first_name` and `last_name` fields instead of `name`, and can now reliably update individual user profile fields via PATCH requests.

userImpact: Users can now reference clear documentation to configure and create custom charts in their dashboards.

summary: Fixed the binary classification dashboard to properly display time gaps in graphs using time_bucket_gapfill for accurate data aggregation. These updates ensure consistency across all dashboard visualizations and prevent misleading visual representations of missing data.
userImpact: Users now see accurate time-series visualizations in the binary classification dashboard, with proper gaps displayed for days when no inferences were recorded, eliminating confusion from missing date intervals.

summary: Implemented lazy deletion for users, allowing user accounts to be marked as deleted without immediate permanent removal. title: UP-1792: Fix db manager deletion bug
summary: Fixed a bug where SpiceDB relationship deletions were not occurring during user deletion because the delete queue was being unexpectedly emptied when `db_manager.flush()` was called. The issue stemmed from SQLAlchemy's weak reference behavior—when objects in the delete queue were moved to the transaction buffer during flush, they were garbage collected, clearing the queue before deletions could be committed to SpiceDB. The fix enqueues deep copies of deleted objects to the delete queue instead of the objects themselves, ensuring they persist through the flush operation.
userImpact: Users can now successfully delete users from groups, and their relationships in SpiceDB are correctly removed during the deletion process.

title: UP-3225: Don't overwrite CSP header on dev

title: unsafe inline into scope

author: martin452

title: Explicit CSP in nginx header
summary: Added an explicit Content Security Policy (CSP) header to the nginx configuration. This resolves CSP-related issues that were preventing proper security policy enforcement on the application.
userImpact: The application now correctly enforces its Content Security Policy, ensuring stricter security controls are in place for user sessions.
author: martin452

title: [UP-3217] fix: modify style-src-elem and script-src-elem
summary: Modified `style-src-elem` and `script-src-elem` Content Security Policy directives in the Vite configuration to address security policy compliance. These directives control where inline styles and scripts can be executed, ensuring the application meets security requirements.
userImpact: Users now experience improved security policy compliance with corrected CSP directives for style and script elements.
author: lukasz94

title: [UP-3200] feat: pass aggregation_kind to model config

title: feat: add CSP plugin & headers

title: fix: field validation and regressions

title: UP-3082: Implement security headers.

title: fix(migration): build FK indexes before deletes; verbose logging
summary: Migration `remove_compliance_schedules` stalled for 40+ minutes due to missing foreign-key indexes on `job_run_id` columns. The fix pre-builds `ix_job_errors_job_run_id` and `ix_job_logs_job_run_id` indexes concurrently before cascade deletes, converting expensive seq-scans to index probes. Batch execution time reduced from minutes to sub-second, with verbose timed logging added for operational visibility.
userImpact: Database migrations now complete significantly faster; the `remove_compliance_schedules` migration that previously stalled for 40+ minutes now completes in minutes with predictable per-batch performance.
author: videetparekh1995

title: fix(migration): batch compliance job deletes outside transaction
summary: Fixed a migration that was causing RDS stalls by performing unbounded deletes on the unindexed jobs.kind column inside a single transaction. The fix implements batched deletes (batch size 100) outside transaction blocks with a temporary concurrent index on jobs.kind, allowing each batch to commit independently and be safely re-run.
userImpact: Database migrations no longer stall on large compliance job deletions, enabling smoother deployment and schema updates.

title: UP-1792: Fix db manager deletion bug
summary: Fixed a critical bug in the user deletion flow where relationships weren't being successfully deleted from SpiceDB. The issue occurred because calling `db_manager.flush()` was unexpectedly emptying the delete queue—when objects are moved from memory to the transaction buffer by SQLAlchemy's session management, external references held in the delete queue become invalid. The fix enqueues deep copies of deleted objects instead of the original references, ensuring deletions remain queued and are properly committed to SpiceDB even after flush operations.
userImpact: Users who are members of groups can now be successfully deleted without orphaned relationship records remaining in SpiceDB.

The fix adds a new PATCH endpoint to update job max_attempts and modifies scheduled job error handling to set max_attempts to the current attempt when unrecoverable errors occur.

title: fix(migration): build FK indexes before deletes; verbose logging
summary: Migration `b7c9066eca19_remove_compliance_schedules` stalled for 40+ minutes on production because cascade-delete FK constraint verifications were performing sequential table scans on large tables (44M and 9.4M rows) lacking appropriate indexes. The fix pre-builds `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` on `job_logs.job_run_id` and `job_errors.job_run_id` before the delete phase, converting constraint verifications from slow sequential scans to fast index probes, reducing batch processing from minutes to sub-second. Added verbose, timed logging for each migration step to enable future diagnosis.
userImpact: The production migration that previously stalled now completes in reasonable time, and operators gain detailed progress visibility into index builds, delete counts, and per-batch timing.
author: videetparekh1995

title: fix(migration): batch compliance job deletes outside transaction
summary: Fixed a migration that was deleting compliance jobs in a single unbounded transaction, causing RDS stalls due to cascade deletes across unindexed `jobs.kind`. The fix batches deletes in groups of 100 using `autocommit_block` with a temporary index on `jobs.kind`, allowing each batch to commit independently and safely re-run without locking the database.
userImpact: Database migrations now complete successfully without causing connection stalls or timeouts when removing compliance schedules on large instances.
author: videetparekh1995

title: UP-2756: Enforce lowercase emails
summary: Fixed a bug where pending invitations were not granted to users with uppercase letters in their email addresses. userImpact: Users invited with uppercase letters in their email address will now successfully accept pending invitations and have their assigned roles granted during sign-up.

userImpact: Aggregation jobs that attempt to use segmentation on columns that don't meet performance requirements will now fail fast with clear validation errors during metrics calculation, preventing downstream performance degradation.

title: UP-2383 fix ownership of upsolve execute patches directory in ECS
summary: Fixed permission denied errors when the upsolve service attempted to access the database patches directory in ECS environments. The `/db-patches` directory was not inheriting the correct ownership from local docker-compose mounts when running in ECS, causing the service to fail with EACCES permission errors when processing patch files.
userImpact: Users running upsolve in ECS can now successfully execute database patches without encountering permission denied errors on the `/db-patches/.executed_files` file.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-2383 upgrade upsolve
summary: Upgraded the upsolve service to the latest version, which includes backend and theme fixes along with read-only mode support. The upgrade was limited to API updates and did not require a fresh export.
userImpact: Users benefit from upsolve backend improvements, theme fixes, and can now use read-only mode when appropriate.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-2423: Handle failure to load datasets in metrics calculation jobs
summary: Updated metrics calculation jobs to gracefully handle failures when loading datasets. When a dataset fails to load, the system now skips metrics calculation for that dataset and provides clear error messaging to users, preventing cascading KeyErrors and improving visibility into root causes of metric failures.
userImpact: Users now see clear error messages when datasets fail to load during metrics calculation, instead of confusing KeyErrors, making it easier to diagnose and resolve data loading issues.
author: alex380125

title: UP-2425: Add datetime information to task connection info
summary: Added datetime information to task connection info to track when connections are created and modified. This enhancement includes a database migration to add timestamp columns to the connection info, updates to the task API models, and changes to the secrets manager and repositories to handle the new datetime fields.
userImpact: Users can now view creation and modification timestamps for task connections, providing better visibility into connection lifecycle and history.
author: alex380125

title: UP-2427 refresh keycloak token during user invite call
summary: Fixed an issue where user invite calls would fail on newly started servers due to missing or expired Keycloak tokens. The token is now refreshed before the invite API call is made, ensuring the authentication is always valid.
userImpact: User invitations now succeed reliably, even when the server has just started and the Keycloak token has not yet been initialized.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-2426 dashboard edit rbac
summary: Added a new `model_edit_dashboard` permission to enable fine-grained role-based access control (RBAC) for dashboard editing. This permission has been integrated into the authorization schema and managed roles, with comprehensive test coverage to ensure proper permission enforcement.
userImpact: Administrators can now control who has access to edit dashboards through RBAC permissions, providing more granular security controls.
author: ianmcgraw

title: UP-2424: Fix regeneration failures
summary: Fixed regeneration failures caused by a recent change that added support for deleting connection info in the control plane. The issue was related to how scheduled deletion of AWS Secrets Manager secrets was being handled—even with ForceDeleteWithoutRecovery enabled, the deletion scheduling logic was interfering with secret regeneration.
userImpact: Connection secret regeneration now completes successfully without failures.
author: alex380125

title: Update dependency redis to v6

This major version includes security improvements and breaking changes to default configurations for SSL hostname checking and cluster client retry behavior.
userImpact: Users can now leverage new hash expiration commands and improved Redis cluster/Sentinel client reliability, though cluster client code may require retry object configuration updates due to breaking changes in default retry behavior.

userImpact: Users now have daily automated backups of the TimeScale database, enabling faster recovery in case of instance failure or data loss.

title: UP-2377 internal connector

The new connector type is hidden from the API response for connector types so it remains internal to the system and is not exposed to the frontend.

title: UP-2315: Update org bootstrap to use immutable org identifier

userImpact: Default organizations are now properly preserved across bootstrap runs, preventing accidental recreation and data inconsistencies when configuration is updated.

title: XP-1556: Add variable to control fetching raw data

The change includes updates to CloudFormation, Docker Compose, and deployment configurations.
userImpact: Administrators can now enable or disable raw data fetching on a per-deployment basis by setting an environment variable, providing better control over data access policies.

title: UP-2291: Create new user via email

This is enabled through new API endpoints and enhanced authorization schema changes including SpiceDB updates.
userImpact: Users can now invite new team members by email and assign them to multiple groups and roles simultaneously, streamlining the user onboarding process without requiring manual password setup.

Deployment logic has been updated to resolve Timescale settings during deployment and pass them to the ECS scope stacks.
userImpact: Users can now configure Timescale connectivity externally, enabling deployments to use bring-your-own Timescale instances instead of relying on the managed Timescale stack dependency.

userImpact: Metrics queries now execute significantly faster as old metric versions are automatically removed during upload, preventing performance degradation experienced by customers like Axios.

userImpact: Users can now safely terminate ECS tasks without losing job state or corrupting data, as the system gracefully waits for in-flight work to complete or cleanly marks it as failed.

title: NO-REF: Change multiprocessing method from fork to spawn
summary: Changed multiprocessing method from fork to spawn to resolve resource sharing issues that occur when forking multithreaded processes (FastAPI/Uvicorn). This eliminates DeprecationWarnings about potential deadlocks and improves CI test stability, though with a modest performance trade-off of ~2 minutes per test suite run in exchange for fewer step failures.
userImpact: CI test suite runs are now more stable with fewer random failures, reducing the need for step restarts despite slightly longer overall execution times.

title: UP-1379 - Add exclude query param to get_jobs endpoint, remove unused job type, lower retry count for scheduled jobs
summary: Added `exclude_kinds` query parameter to the `get_jobs` endpoint, allowing callers to filter out specific job types from results. The parameter takes precedence over `kinds`, so specifying both for the same job type will exclude it. Also removed an unused duplicate job type for data retrieval and fixed a Postgres compatibility issue by lowering the scheduled job retry count from values exceeding Postgres's 32-bit integer limit.
userImpact: Users can now exclude specific job types from queries using the `exclude_kinds` parameter, and the API no longer returns 500 errors for scheduled jobs in Postgres environments.

title: UP-1410: add upsolve monitoring support
summary: Added upsolve service monitoring support to the CloudFormation monitoring dashboard and alarms. The integration leverages dynamic dashboard updates for most charts and adds explicit metric calculations for rate charts and log views. Alarms are configured following AWS best practices for ECS Container Insights RunningTaskCount metrics.

userImpact: Schedule jobs will no longer be exhausted and halted after a finite number of retries, allowing schedules to recover automatically when the system returns to normal operation.

title: UP-1468 | Add default order by id to queries
summary: Adds a secondary order_by clause on id to database queries for alerts to ensure consistent, deterministic pagination results when primary sort fields contain non-unique values. This prevents unpredictable result ordering that could occur when multiple records share the same sort key.
userImpact: Users will now receive consistent and predictable pagination results when querying alerts, eliminating inconsistent ordering that previously occurred with non-unique sort fields.

title: UP-1528 add default limit and page size for raw data retrieval job

The Shield connector now respects a configurable limit parameter and translates it internally to page size, making the defaults connector-agnostic and future-proof for other storage backends.
userImpact: Raw data retrieval jobs now fetch a reasonable subset of data by default instead of all available data, preventing excessive memory and processing overhead when users don't explicitly specify a limit.

title: UP-4362 Typed routes refactor
summary: Introduces a centralized, type-safe route dictionary (`paths`) that replaces hardcoded URL strings and untyped navigation primitives throughout the codebase. All route builders return a branded `RoutePath` type, and new wrapper components (`AppLink`, `useAppNavigate`, `useNavigateWithFrom`, `appRedirect`) enforce type safety at compile time. An ESLint rule prevents raw `react-router-dom` imports in the app, ensuring all future navigation goes through the typed system.
userImpact: Developers can now define and navigate routes with full type safety, eliminating URL construction errors and making route changes automatically checked by TypeScript across the entire codebase.

title: UP-4088 alert rules navigation 500 error
summary: Fixed an intermittent 500 error when clicking "Back to Alerts" on the Alert Rules Management page. The root cause was that model and alert rule loaders failed to clear both `workspaceId` and `projectId` consistently from the store on route resolution failures, leaving stale project IDs that produced malformed back URLs. Added `setProjectId(null)` to catch blocks in both `modelLoader.tsx` and `alertRuleLoader.tsx` to ensure both IDs are always cleared together.

userImpact: Users will now see accurate counts of total engines and actively running engines in the Workspace Dashboard, with reliable health status detection across the application.

title: fix(users): skip UPDATE when no fields changed
summary: The `authed_user` FastAPI dependency was unconditionally running UPDATE queries on the `users` table on every authenticated request, regardless of whether any user metadata actually changed. This generated excessive write load, database multixact churn, and SLRU cache misses on Aurora PostgreSQL. The fix short-circuits the UPDATE when no user fields differ from the existing row.
userImpact: Users will experience improved API response times and reduced database latency as unnecessary UPDATE operations on the users table are eliminated.
author: ianmcgraw

title: perf(jobs): add partial dequeue index
summary: Added a partial index on the jobs table to accelerate the job dequeue polling query. The index covers only active jobs (queued or running state, ~0.66% of the table) and is pre-sorted by dequeue order, reducing query execution from 225ms with 207MB of buffer reads to 0.008ms with minimal buffer access.
userImpact: Job polling becomes significantly faster, reducing per-worker polling latency and decreasing database load from continuous table scans.
author: ianmcgraw

title: feat(shared-components): add slot props + render splits to trace viewer for task tour
summary: Enhanced the trace viewer component in shared-components by adding slot props support and render splits functionality to the TraceDrawerBody and related trace components. This enables more flexible customization and improved rendering capabilities for the task tour feature.
userImpact: Users can now customize trace viewer rendering with slot props and leverage render splits for enhanced task tour interactions in the trace visualization interface.

userImpact: Users benefit from bug fixes and improvements included in upsolve 0.4.30.
author: ianmcgraw

title: Claude Code Observability - Fix sub agent spans hierarchy + more tests
summary: Fixed three critical issues preventing subagent spans from nesting correctly under their parent AGENT spans in distributed traces. The fixes address: programmatic subagents (Explore-type) that bypass UserPromptSubmit and never inherit parent context; race conditions where UserPromptSubmit overwrites the pre_tool-inherited trace_id and parent_agent_span_id; and collisions in parallel Agent/Task calls sharing the same pending span ID. Extended Task tool to use the same span hierarchy logic as Agent, and added comprehensive end-to-end trace tests with InMemorySpanExporter to verify span parent-child relationships.
userImpact: Subagent traces are now correctly nested under their parent traces, enabling proper observability of multi-level agent workflows. Concurrent agent calls no longer collide, and programmatic agents (without user prompts) correctly inherit trace context from their parent.
author: ntatsumi

title: feat(multitenancy): Pattern C — org_scope filtering on read paths (UP-4429)
summary: Implements Pattern C multi-tenancy filtering across 92 task-scoped repository endpoints, ensuring tenant callers receive 404 (instead of cross-org resource leakage) on unauthorized reads. Adds org_scope parameter to all task-scoped repository lookup methods and wires filtering across 17 router files. Completes comprehensive endpoint audit: all 193 OpenAPI operations now have protection via Pattern A/C/D/E decorators and repository filtering with zero unprotected endpoints.
userImpact: Tenant users can no longer access or infer existence of other organizations' tasks, inferences, spans, traces, datasets, experiments, and notebooks; admins remain unaffected.
author: mcgrawia

title: feat: add Azure Blob Storage connector for ml-engine
summary: Added a new Azure Blob Storage connector for ml-engine that supports four authentication methods: connection string, service principal, SAS token, and account key with account name. The connector wraps `adlfs.AzureBlobFileSystem` and extends `BucketBasedConnector` to provide unified file-based read operations. Comprehensive unit tests cover all authentication paths, validation errors, and read scenarios including pagination and column filtering.
userImpact: Users can now connect to Azure Blob Storage in ml-engine workflows using any of four authentication methods and perform file read operations seamlessly.
author: iabouhashish

title: fix: restore definition field on TraceTransformResponse from latest version
summary: Restores the `definition` field on `TraceTransformResponse` that was inadvertently lost during versioning introduction. The field is now populated from the latest `TraceTransformVersion`, ensuring existing API callers continue to receive transform definitions without breaking changes. Added batch definition fetching to eliminate N+1 queries across all transform-returning routes.
userImpact: API consumers can now access the `definition` field on all transform endpoints (`GET`, `POST`, `PATCH /transforms`) just as before, with no changes required to existing code.
author: iabouhashish

title: feat(multitenancy): public tenant signup endpoint (UP-4430)
summary: Implements a public tenant signup endpoint `POST /api/v2/tenant/signup` that atomically creates an organization, task, and API key in a single transaction when demo mode is enabled. The endpoint is gated by `GENAI_ENGINE_DEMO_MODE` and returns a four-field response containing org ID, task ID, task name, and the raw API key. Supporting repository changes add backward-compatible `commit` kwargs to enable atomic multi-step operations.
userImpact: Users can now self-serve sign up for a demo tenant via a single public API endpoint that provisions a complete org, task, and API key in one transaction.
author: videetparekh

title: feat(multitenancy): enforce org scope on routes (UP-4425)
summary: Implements API-level enforcement of organization scope for genai-engine routes, preventing tenant-scoped callers from accessing tasks belonging to other organizations. Two new decorators (`@enforce_org_scope()` for path-based task IDs and `@enforce_query_org_scope()` for query parameters) are applied across 60+ path-based and 11 query-based endpoints, with org_id denormalized onto child rows at write time to support efficient filtering. Admin callers bypass these checks unchanged.
userImpact: Tenant-scoped API callers are now isolated to their organization's tasks and cannot access or enumerate tasks from other organizations; admin callers retain full access.
author: mcgrawia

title: feat(multitenancy): GET /users/me identity introspection (UP-4426)
summary: Adds `GET /users/me` endpoint to return the current user's identity and organizational scope. This new endpoint returns user_id, roles, org_scope, and org details, with defensive handling for deleted orgs. The endpoint differentiates between admin API keys (org_scope=null), tenant API keys (org_scope and org populated), and JWT authentication, filling the gap identified in UP-4426 design specification §6.
userImpact: The UI can now call `GET /users/me` to determine the user's identity and organizational context, enabling it to render appropriate admin vs. tenant branches on login.
author: videetparekh

title: feat(multitenancy): add TENANT-USER role + permission frozensets (UP-4428)
summary: Added `TENANT-USER` role with granular permission frozensets to enable tenant API keys to access read/write surfaces aligned with multi-tenancy scope. Carved out `TRACES_WRITE` as admin-only to prevent inadvertent trace ingest access from broader `INFERENCE_WRITE` permission, while permitting tenants to annotate traces. Admin API key creation now explicitly rejects `TENANT-USER` role, enforcing signup-flow-only provisioning model.
userImpact: Tenant API keys can now authenticate and call permitted endpoints (task/inference/feedback operations, model provider metadata, usage reports, trace annotations) while remaining locked out of administrative functions and trace ingest.
author: videetparekh

title: add ability to create demo task
summary: Adds the ability to create and interact with a demo task when the feature flag is enabled. The demo task includes a prompt, sample continuous evaluations (one passing, one intentionally incorrect for user fixes), example datasets with Q&A pairs, and traces with evaluation results. Refactors chatbot architecture to store conversation history on the frontend and pass the entire history to the backend with each request, eliminating the need for in-memory caching.

title: CI failure: yarn install --immutable checksum mismatch
summary: Fixed a CI checksum mismatch failure by switching @tanstack/react-form from a mutable PR-number URL to an immutable commit-SHA URL. By pinning to the specific commit SHA (3aac089), the dependency is now content-addressed and immutable, preventing future checksum drift.

title: ci: rebuild the models-gcs image only when its inputs change
summary: Added `has_updates` gate to the `build-gcp-model-upload-docker-image` CI job, matching the behavior of its S3 and filesystem counterparts. This prevents unnecessary rebuilds of the 7.25 GB models-gcs image when only version bumps occur without actual model or build-input changes. Over six months, this will reduce ~450 version bumps to ~19 warranted rebuilds by re-tagging existing images instead.
userImpact: No direct user impact. CI infrastructure will now skip redundant image builds when model inputs are unchanged, improving build efficiency and reducing resource consumption.
author: ntatsumi

title: ci: re-scan images when the VEX changes
summary: Added a `push` trigger on `dev` branch scoped to `security/vex/openvex.json` in the image vulnerability scan workflow, so triage decisions in the VEX file take effect immediately at merge time rather than waiting for the next scheduled nightly run. This eliminates delays in closing suppressed Trivy alerts, particularly for model images that use registry-to-registry re-tagging without a scan step.
userImpact: Vulnerability triages and suppressions defined in the VEX file now take effect immediately when merged to dev, rather than waiting up to 24 hours for the next scheduled scan.

title: ci: scan the models images at build time, not only overnight
